svg.text: S2 ONE SHAFT, ONE CAR — worst case: bottom level, rear box
A car in the empty middle shaft pins the box, pulls it sideways onto its deck, lifts it and pushes it into the hand-over cell.
worst case: L1 (bottom), rear box, right lane → hand-over cell R
≈ 11.5 s real time · mean ≈ 7 s · put-away ≤ 7.5 s (≤ 17 s with compaction)
no other box is ever moved: no digging, no shuffling
3 motors for the whole column: Z (car), Y (carriage), X (toe)
ZOOM: the car and the box (section through the car, 0.9 px/mm)

g.text: car drops 10 mm: pin in slot

svg.text: car down 1,678 mm ∥ toe to y, x
car drops 10 mm: pin in slot
car up 1,668 mm ∥ slide to front

g.text: 1/9 Command. The car is parked empty at the top (load cell reads 0). Target: L1, right lane, rear box.
2/9 The car goes down 1.68 m to 10 mm above L1. Meanwhile the toe moves to the box position (Y) and to the right shaft edge (X).
3/9 The toe reaches 13 mm into the lane, under the flange. An IR sensor finds the rib.
4/9 The whole car drops 10 mm: the pin goes through the slot in the rib. The NFC tag in the rib is read.
5/9 Pull 182 mm sideways: the box slides over the 3 mm gap onto the car deck. The load cell checks the mass.
6/9 Up 1.67 m to the hand-over level H. At the same time the toe slides the box along the car to the front.
7/9 Push 182 mm into hand-over cell R, against its outer stop.
8/9 The car rises 10 mm (pin out of the slot) and the toe goes back into the shaft.
9/9 Sensor: box in cell R. The transport is told and lifts it through the ceiling port.
Done in ≈ 11.5 s real time. No other box was touched: every box stands next to the shaft.
